story: At 8:17 on this sunny Friday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary has just pulled his cornbread from the oven at home and is wrapping it up for Rosa's dinner. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is straightening her plastic flamingo flock from the curb and tucking one stray bird behind the hedge so that exactly three show, while Hal grudgingly accepts the arrangement with a nod. Rosa, feeling hopeful, is keeping the sides warm in her kitchen and listening for the doorbell so she can greet her guests.
events: Gary (gary fridge): Pull the finished cornbread out of the oven and wrap it up for Rosa's dinner
Donna (donna flamingo flock): Check the flock from the curb and tuck any stray bird behind the hedge so exactly three show
Rosa waited: Stay by the kitchen keeping the sides warm and listening for the doorbell, so I can greet Gary, Donna, and Hal as they arrive.

gary.thought_process: The cornbread went into the oven last tick, so it should be about done by now, and I promised it to Rosa for Friday's dinner. I'm alone at home with the fridge right here, but the oven's the thing to check. Cart modifications stay parked until Hal signs off on the Architectural Review filing, so the workbench can wait. Best move now is to pull the cornbread out and get it ready to carry over, which keeps my word and keeps me useful to the neighbors.

parameters.content: Pull the finished cornbread out of the oven and wrap it up for Rosa's dinner

donna.thought_process: Hal is out here counting the flamingos again. I already moved the extras behind the hedge and told him so, and I've waited an hour since. There's no sense repeating myself. Best thing is to go look at the flock myself so I know the street really sees exactly three, and then I can settle it with Hal and get on with Rosa's dinner and my pickleball plans with Gary.

parameters.content: Check the flock from the curb and tuck any stray bird behind the hedge so exactly three show

hal.thought_process: Donna says she moved the extras behind the hedge and asked me to count again. I've been staring at that flock for two ticks, and by the book it's three visible from the street, which is within L-02. I'm not one to pretend a violation exists when it doesn't. Besides, Rosa's dinner is tonight and Donna's been decent about this. Gary's cart paperwork is still unresolved, but that's a separate matter for later. I'll give her an honest answer and put the flamingo business to bed.

parameters.content: Counted three from the street, Donna. That's the limit and you're on it, so no report from me. Keep it that way and we'll get along fine at Rosa's tonight.

rosa.thought_process: It's 8:17 PM and everything is set: table laid with the good plates, sides warm, schedule checked. No guests are in sight yet, and I've already done the final fixes on the napkins and centerpiece over the last few ticks. Fussing again would just be repeating myself. Best to stay put near the kitchen, keep the food warm, and be ready to open the door the moment Gary, Donna, and Hal arrive.

parameters.content: Stay by the kitchen keeping the sides warm and listening for the doorbell, so I can greet Gary, Donna, and Hal as they arrive.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
